channel.title: Columbia Journalism Review - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Columbia Journalism Review (cjr.org)

item.title: What Happened to Trump’s Biggest Fan?
item.description: As Marjorie Taylor Greene contemplates her next move, her betrothed, a Trump-friendly broadcaster named Brian Glenn, is adjusting to life on the outside.

item.title: Ali Breland on Why It’s Important to Cover the Online Far Right
item.description: An Atlantic reporter says far-right influencers such as Nick Fuentes offer clues to where US politics is going.

item.title: Mending Local News in a Crisis
item.description: How nonprofit and for-profit business models can complement each other when big-money media fails.

item.title: Profit or Nonprofit? A Debate over Journalism’s Future
item.description: While the newspaper industry continues to contract, nonprofit news outlets have proliferated over the past decade. But dismissing profitable models for journalism is premature.

item.title: What We Need to Know
item.description: Ann Curry reports from Sudan. Plus: Second-person scenarios, and AI mayhem.

item.title: Trump’s EPA Wants Us to Cover Our Eyes
item.description: On climate policy, the Trump administration is willfully burying its head in the sand. It’s crucial newsrooms don’t follow.

item.title: NewsNation’s Moment
item.description: As Nexstar, its corporate parent, pursues a merger with Tegna, NewsNation goes after the Nancy Guthrie story.

item.title: The Voice of the Uyghur Post
item.description: A Uyghur-language news site is aiming to connect a scattered diaspora and preserve a culture at risk of disappearing.

item.title: In This Cleveland Newsroom, AI Is Writing (But Not Reporting) the News
item.description: Cleveland.com is embracing AI tools, including an AI rewrite desk.

item.title: Taking Reality TV Seriously
item.description: Trump brought drama. Bravo sheds light. Brian Moylan has seen and covered it all.
